title: Rapid capacity priming, queue pruning, and admission-control follow-up for hosted GPU exhaustion
creator: Priya Singh
description:
Summary: This ticket captures the engineering follow-ups from the hosted-GPU exhaustion incident on 2025-02-12 where sustained queue buildup caused elevated tail latency and a partial throttling spiral. The focus is on three pragmatic mitigations that can be implemented in the next release window: (1) capacity priming (warm pools + proactive instance provisioning), (2) queue pruning & eviction policies to bound amplification during bursts, and (3) admission-control refactor to fast-fail or reroute low-value traffic and prioritize short-running requests.

Background & root cause hypotheses: During the incident we observed a compound failure mode: sudden workload spike from a downstream partner + a conservative autoscaler hysteresis that delayed new GPU allocation by ~90–180s + a KV-cache thrash pattern that prevented effective prefix reuse. This led to sustained queue growth and head-of-line blocking where a few long-running requests consumed most throughput. Existing admission control favored accepting requests and queuing them rather than failing fast, which amplified the backlog.

Goals for this ticket:
- Reduce time-to-capacity for sudden bursts via pool warmers and priming heuristics.
- Limit queue amplification with a deterministic eviction policy and short priority lanes.
- Implement admission-control rules that detect low-probability high-cost requests and either fast-fail or route to cheaper model variants.
- Add measurable SLOs and dashboards for burst handling: queue length P95/P99, provisioning lag, and eviction rate.
- Update runbooks and postmortem artifacts; schedule a chaos test to validate changes before canary.

Success criteria (measurable):
- 95th-percentile provisioning lag <= 30s in synthetic burst test.
- Queue amplification ratio (enqueued/permitted) reduced by >= 4x under load tests.
- Tail request latency (P99) reduced by >= 50% for affected routes in canary.
- No customer-facing errors attributable to aggressive admission heuristics during a 72-hour canary window.
updates: 2025-02-18 - Priya Singh: Created ticket after incident postmortem; baseline metrics attached. Action items split into short, medium, long term.

2025-02-20 - Marcelo Rivera: Prototype capacity priming implemented in dev; warm pool controller added with a conservative default (2x baseline for flagged routes). Initial load test shows provisioning lag down from ~120s to ~35s.
2025-02-24 - SRE Team (Zoe Chen): Observed cache cold-start pattern causing repeated KV misses; recommended pre-warming of common prefixes and adding KV cache metrics to dashboards.

2025-02-26 - Marcelo Rivera: Queue-pruning design reviewed with PM and Design. Chosen approach: priority lanes (short/long), eviction by estimated token-cost, and backoff window for requeue. Draft PR opened.

2025-03-02 - Priya Singh: Admission-control policy spec approved in engineering review (see links). Plan to canary admission rules on a small subset of hostnames next week; runbook updated with rollback triggers.
2025-03-02 - Marcelo Rivera: Estimate revised to 8 points after factoring integration work with autoscaler and runtime kernel selection; added dependency on load-sim infra ticket.
comments: Asha Patel (PM) 2025-02-19: Prioritize customer routes that experienced the outage for priming. Let's create a short list of top 10 high-value hostnames to be targeted in the first rollout.
Liam O'Connor (Design) 2025-02-21: UX for the console alert needs an explicit 'priming active' flag and a way to opt-out for specific customers — added to labels.
Ethan Park (SRE) 2025-02-25: PR feedback: ensure warm pool controller respects Dedicated capacity reservations and doesn't try to over-provision shared hosted GPUs. Added a guard and config flag.

Natalie Ruiz (Infra) 2025-02-26: Load generator script updated to simulate KV-cache thrash; results attached in Grafana snapshot link. We should run a 2h soak at 2x normal burst profile before canary.
Zoe Chen (SRE) 2025-03-01: Runbook: added explicit rollback conditions — if provisioning lag > 60s or eviction rate > 30% for 10m, revert admission heuristics and disable priming for affected pool.
Marcelo Rivera 2025-03-02: Code review notes resolved for PR #4976; waiting on infra approval to merge and schedule canary.
